- The only explicit hard constraints from the problem statement are: every model must be assigned to an available GPU; for every GPU, total `model_size` must fit in GPU memory; and the intended objective is to minimize the maximum GPU KVPR, where

- Under the stated objective, the largest lever is reducing the *largest* resulting KVPR, not minimizing total KVPR, average KVPR, unused memory, assignment runtime, or number of used GPUs. - There is an inherent packing/balancing conflict: consolidating models may conserve empty GPUs but sharply reduces denominator slack and raises KVPR; spreading models protects denominator slack but consumes capacity on more GPUs. Large model sizes are especially costly on nearly full GPUs, while high `req_rate / slo` models are especially costly on GPUs already carrying high request-pressure sums.
- No simplicity, runtime, deterministic-output, or placement-stability score is visible in the supplied evaluator wrapper. “Simple as possible” is a problem-description preference, not a confirmed evaluator reward. Do not trade measurable max-KVPR quality for cosmetic simplification unless hidden evaluation imposes a runtime limit.

If it receives the normal full collections of models and GPUs—as model-placement functions commonly do—this is an offline/batch optimization problem: sort globally, inspect all placements, run local search, and use global optimization; it need not be causal or streaming. If calls instead arrive incrementally, preserve a fast greedy fallback, but do not assume that restriction without inspecting the hidden interface.

strategy_diverge_guidance:

- Exact feasibility-under-threshold search; binary-search a candidate maximum KVPR and test assignments satisfying per-GPU `pressure_sum <= threshold * (memory - size_sum)` plus memory feasibility. For small instances, use `scipy.optimize.milp` with integrality constraints to obtain globally strong batch placements; this directly targets evaluator-visible maximum KVPR.
- Mixed-integer minimax formulation; use `scipy.optimize.milp` with binary model-to-GPU assignment variables and an auxiliary maximum-KVPR threshold variable, with linearized threshold-feasibility constraints for a fixed threshold. This is global rather than greedy and preserves one-GPU-per-model and memory constraints.
- Deterministic bottleneck-aware greedy; sort models by a combined difficulty measure such as high `req_rate / slo`, large `model_size`, or estimated marginal KVPR increase, then assign each to the feasible GPU yielding the smallest resulting maximum KVPR. Replacement scope: Replace the complete greedy-construction and relocation/swap loop inside `compute_model_placement` with a fixed-threshold mixed-integer feasibility search, retaining the current greedy placement only as the finite upper-bound and solver-failure fallback.

Mechanism family: recursive-capacity-bisection  
Replacement scope: Replace the four `orders`/`construct(order)` seed-generation phase with one additional recursive bisection seed generator, retaining the existing greedy construction as the guaranteed fallback and retaining the downstream MILP phase.  
Compute budget: One recursive partition tree with at most `gpu_num - 1` internal nodes; at each node use at most 12 deterministic candidate split points after sorting by transformed pressure-density. Expected evaluation-time effect: negligible for ordinary model counts and no optimizer starts.  
Gain mechanism: Partition the GPU set recursively into left and right groups of nearly equal cardinality. At a node with `q` GPUs and model set `S`, estimate the current threshold using total pressure divided by total available residual memory, score each model by `pressure + threshold * size`, sort by that score, and choose a split whose two sides fit their aggregate memory capacities while making transformed load proportional to the number of GPUs. Recurse until single GPUs, then validate every leaf. This gives a global cut topology: high transformed-load models are separated before greedy destination choices can consume the slack needed by them. If any subtree cannot be made capacity-feasible, discard this seed and use the existing feasible greedy seed. Every accepted leaf is checked to have total size below 80 GB and every original model appears in exactly one leaf.  
Expected-gain check: recursive cuts permit coordinated separation of several high-pressure/high-size models across disjoint GPU groups, a placement degree of freedom absent from sequential greedy placement; retain the seed only if it yields a hidden combined score above 26.2559717495.

strategies.title: ordered attempt [genetic-bin-crossover] Feasible group-preserving island crossover
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: genetic-bin-crossover  
Replacement scope: Replace the single best-seed handoff to MILP with a bounded population stage operating on the existing four greedy seeds, then pass its best feasible result to the existing threshold MILP.  
Compute budget: Population size 8, at most 5 generations, at most 8 crossover children per generation, and at most one greedy repair scan per child. Expected evaluation-time effect: bounded moderate increase, with no additional external solver calls.  
Gain mechanism: Canonicalize each parent by sorting GPU bins by `(KVPR, used memory, contents)`. Form a child by retaining alternating whole GPU bins from parent A, removing their models from parent B, then inserting all remaining models in parent-B bin order into the child’s open GPUs using exact resulting-max-KVPR destination selection. This transfers coherent low-pressure/large-memory bin configurations rather than individual local moves. Reject a child immediately if greedy repair cannot fit all remaining models, and retain only feasible children with a strictly better full descending KVPR objective. Canonical bin handling avoids GPU-label artifacts; repairs preserve one assignment per model and reject any memory overflow.  
Expected-gain check: whole-bin crossover can combine compatible capacity patterns from different greedy orderings that neither parent nor a one-model move can construct, so it is falsifiably useful only if resulting hidden combined score exceeds 26.2559717495.

strategies.title: [tabu-trajectory-descent] Bottleneck tabu relocation-and-swap search
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: tabu-trajectory-descent

Replacement scope: Replace the final `return` phase after the MILP bisection block with a bounded assignment-level tabu search initialized from the best greedy/MILP incumbent; retain the existing greedy and MILP phases unchanged as seed generators.

Compute budget: One deterministic tabu trajectory of at most 80 accepted moves; inspect relocations from either of the two currently highest-KVPR GPUs to every feasible destination and swaps involving models on those GPUs. Maintain a tabu tenure of 7 accepted moves for reversed model-GPU assignments, with aspiration when a candidate improves the best-ever lexicographic KVPR vector. Expected evaluation-time effect: modest additional Python work, normally below the existing repeated MILP cost.

Gain mechanism: The present code accepts only independently feasible threshold-MILP solutions and has no mechanism for deliberately crossing a locally worse assignment to unlock a lower bottleneck later. Tabu memory adds a directed search trajectory over assignment space: it can temporarily worsen the maximum KVPR, forbid immediate reversal, and subsequently exploit capacity released on a previously congested GPU. Every candidate computes exact affected GPU memory and pressure totals, rejects any total size above 80 GB, and only returns the best feasible state found.

Represent each state by `bins`, `used`, and `weight`; rank states by the full descending KVPR vector already used by the parent. At each step, generate feasible relocation and swap candidates touching a current bottleneck GPU, choose the best non-tabu candidate by that vector, update the tabu expiry for the reverse assignment, and preserve the globally best feasible state separately. A relocation is legal only if its destination stays within memory; a swap is legal only if both resulting GPU sizes stay within memory. Return the best-ever state, never merely the final tabu state.

Expected-gain check: this is falsifiable by requiring hidden evaluation to report `max_kvpr < 25.2559717495`; the new degree of freedom is a bounded non-improving, non-reversible assignment trajectory, which the incumbent’s independently accepted greedy and feasibility-bisection states cannot traverse.

strategies.title: [quartet-clique-reoptimization] Four-GPU restricted exact repartitioning
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: quartet-clique-reoptimization

Replacement scope: Replace the single global MILP-bisection improvement block with a seed-plus-quartet refinement phase: retain greedy construction, then reoptimize selected four-GPU induced subproblems while all models outside the selected GPUs remain fixed.

Compute budget: At most 3 quartet selections per input; for each quartet, at most 10 threshold probes and one `scipy.optimize.milp` call per probe, each with a 0.10-second time limit. Expected evaluation-time effect: bounded near the current global-bisection budget, with smaller MILPs when the instance has many GPUs.

Gain mechanism: Rather than repeatedly asking a short global MILP solve to decide every model-to-GPU variable simultaneously, this creates a dense four-way exchange clique around the actual bottleneck. The models currently resident on four selected GPUs may be assigned to any of the four GPUs, allowing coordinated rotations and combinations that single greedy choices cannot create. The quartet topology is materially different from a pair exchange: three donor/receiver relationships can be used while a fourth GPU provides temporary memory slack.

Start from the best greedy seed. Form quartets deterministically from the highest-KVPR GPU, the next two highest-KVPR GPUs, and the lowest-KVPR GPU with useful free memory; use alternate quartets by replacing one middle member with the next-ranked GPU. For each quartet, freeze every assignment outside it, collect only models currently inside it, and solve threshold feasibility for their four assignment choices. Constraints are exactly one selected-GPU assignment per collected model, size total at most 80 GB per selected GPU, and `pressure_sum + T * size_sum <= 80 * T` after including fixed outside loads (which are zero for selected GPUs under this induced formulation). Decode only integral one-hot assignments and recompute all KVPRs before accepting a lexicographically better state. If no feasible solve improves, preserve the original incumbent.

Expected-gain check: require `max_kvpr < 25.2559717495` on hidden evaluation; this check is falsifiable, and the added degree of freedom is an exact four-bin simultaneous repartition, which is absent from the parent’s one-pass constructions and is not represented by a single local move.

strategies.title: [beam-frontier-packing] Canonical partial-packing beam search
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: beam-frontier-packing

Replacement scope: Replace the four `construct(order)` greedy seed constructions with a canonical beam-search constructor, while keeping the existing post-construction MILP block as an optional final refinement.

Compute budget: Use two deterministic difficulty orderings, beam width 24, and expand at most `24 * gpu_num` child placements per model per ordering; deduplicate states by sorted per-GPU `(used_memory, pressure_sum, member-index tuple)` signatures. Expected evaluation-time effect: predictable `O(48 * n * gpu_num)` candidate expansion, generally small relative to 18 MILP calls.

Gain mechanism: The current construction irrevocably commits every model to one locally best GPU. Beam packing retains multiple geometrically distinct partial memory layouts, including layouts that are initially inferior in KVPR but reserve the correct slack profile for large later models. Canonicalizing GPU labels removes symmetric duplicates, so beam capacity is spent on genuinely different partitions rather than relabelings.

For each ordering—descending `(model_size, pressure)` and descending `(pressure / max(model_size, epsilon), model_size)`—begin with the all-empty state. For each next model, extend every retained state by assigning that model to every GPU with resulting size at most 80 GB. Canonicalize GPU labels by sorting bins on `(used_memory, pressure_sum, sorted model indices)` before deduplication. Rank partial states using a lower-risk completion key: descending current KVPR vector, then descending used memory vector, then total squared current KVPR; retain the best 24 distinct feasible states. After all models are assigned, use the exact full descending KVPR vector to choose the beam incumbent. Every generated state assigns each processed model exactly once and rejects memory violations immediately.

Expected-gain check: require `max_kvpr < 25.2559717495` on hidden evaluation; the falsifiable new degree of freedom is retention of up to 24 incompatible partial memory-slack arrangements per prefix, whereas each incumbent `construct` retains exactly one arrangement for that prefix.

strategies.title: [circulating-exchange-neighborhood] Exact simultaneous one-outflow GPU circulati
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: circulating-exchange-neighborhood

Replacement scope: Replace the current post-bisection return path with a deterministic polishing phase applied to the best greedy/MILP incumbent before formatting the result.

Compute budget: At most 3 neighborhood solves; each solve uses one MILP feasibility bisection of 10 threshold steps, with a 0.05-second solver limit per step. Expected evaluation-time effect: small, because the neighborhood contains at most two exportable models per GPU rather than every model.

Gain mechanism: The current construction and threshold MILP can leave a placement trapped behind a coordinated exchange: moving any one model into a destination GPU is infeasible or increases its KVPR, while moving one model out of that destination at the same time makes the whole circulation beneficial. Build a restricted exchange MILP from the current placement by selecting, for every GPU, its two models with greatest bottleneck-relief score `pressure / remaining_memory` and allowing only those selected models to move. All nonselected models remain fixed. The restricted MILP has one assignment variable per selected model and GPU, preserves exact model assignment, and uses residual per-GPU memory and pressure in its threshold constraints. Solve it for the smallest threshold; accept the decoded solution only if its exact sorted KVPR vector improves the incumbent. Repeat with selection scores based respectively on pressure, model size, and `pressure + incumbent_max * size`.

Every candidate remains valid because each selected model receives exactly one destination, every fixed model remains on its original GPU, and residual memory plus moved-model memory is constrained to at most 80 GB per GPU. Expected-gain check: this exposes simultaneous directed cycles of model transfers that the incumbent’s retained greedy solution has no dedicated repair phase to construct; it passes the falsifiable evaluator check only if `max_kvpr < 25.2559717495`.

strategies.title: [ratio-contact-block-coordinate] Ratio-contact component reoptimization
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: ratio-contact-block-coordinate

Replacement scope: Replace the four fixed greedy seed constructions with a component-based seed-and-improve phase; retain the existing global threshold MILP as the final fallback/global improvement stage.

Compute budget: Build at most 2 GPU contact components per incumbent and solve at most 2 component MILPs, each with 12 threshold steps and a 0.06-second limit per step. Components are capped at 6 GPUs. Expected evaluation-time effect: bounded modest increase, with substantially smaller MILPs than the full assignment solve.

Gain mechanism: Start from the best deterministic greedy placement. Rank GPUs by current KVPR and form a contact graph in which each high-KVPR GPU is connected to feasible recipient GPUs whose post-insertion KVPR is lowest after temporarily removing one influential model from the high-KVPR GPU. Grow a capped component from the current worst GPU by repeatedly adding its strongest contact. Remove all models in that component, retain all placements outside it, and exactly reassign the component’s models among its component GPUs with a threshold MILP using the fixed outside loads as offsets. This differs from fixed-size GPU subsets because the subsystem topology is induced by actual feasible pressure-relief contacts; it can include a chain such as bottleneck → recipient → recipient’s recipient, instead of requiring all relief to occur inside an arbitrary pair, triple, or quartet.

Hard constraints are preserved by retaining every outside assignment unchanged, assigning every component model exactly once, and enforcing each component GPU’s full memory limit including fixed outside load. Expected-gain check: the method can improve placements requiring a pressure-relief chain across an irregular 4–6 GPU contact component, a topology not selected by the incumbent’s global greedy seeds; retain it only if evaluator measurement yields `max_kvpr < 25.2559717495`.

strategies.title: [canonical-dominance-branch-search] Symmetry-reduced exact threshold branch sear
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: canonical-dominance-branch-search

Replacement scope: Replace the current SciPy threshold-bisection block for small and medium instances (`n <= 28`) and retain the existing MILP block for larger instances or if the node budget is reached.

Compute budget: At most 80,000 depth-first assignment nodes for each of 14 bisection thresholds; no external optimizer starts. Expected evaluation-time effect: predictable bounded CPU work on small/medium cases and no change on larger cases.

Gain mechanism: For a fixed candidate threshold `T`, use the equivalent capacity inequality `sum(pressure + T * size) <= 80*T` per GPU. Branch models in descending order of `max(size / 80, (pressure + T*size)/(80*T))`, which places the most restrictive model first. At each depth, maintain each GPU’s `(used_memory, threshold_load)` pair. Canonicalize interchangeable GPUs by trying only one representative of each equal rounded state, and prune states dominated by a previously seen canonical vector whose sorted GPU states have no greater used memory and no greater threshold load. Also prune when the sum of remaining model sizes cannot fit into aggregate residual capacity, or when any unassigned model fits in no GPU. The first complete placement certifies threshold feasibility; bisection narrows from the greedy incumbent threshold.

This changes the representation from a generic binary MILP to a canonical packing state search that removes GPU-label symmetry and retains strong partial-state dominance, allowing it to reach feasible thresholds that repeated short time-limited MILPs may not find. Every branch adds a model to exactly one GPU only when memory remains within 80 GB, so all returned leaves are valid placements. Expected-gain check: this is falsifiable by running the bounded search on `n <= 28` instances and requiring its returned placement to achieve `max_kvpr < 25.2559717495`; otherwise the greedy/MILP incumbent is retained.

strategies.title: [sensitivity-matched-permutation] Simultaneous marginal-cost permutation refinem
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: sensitivity-matched-permutation

Replacement scope: Replace the current post-construction incumbent-selection phase before the MILP bisection block; retain the greedy constructors and MILP fallback.

Compute budget: At most 12 refinement rounds per incumbent, with one bipartite assignment solve per round over at most one selected model from each GPU; expected evaluation-time effect is small because each round uses an at-most-`gpu_num × gpu_num` cost matrix.

Gain mechanism: The incumbent can test only a threshold-feasibility MILP solution and does not deliberately coordinate simultaneous relocations among several GPUs. This refinement removes one sensitivity-selected model from each GPU, computes the exact resulting KVPR after inserting that model into every other GPU, then solves a minimum-bottleneck permutation so several GPUs can exchange models simultaneously. Unlike isolated relocation or pair swapping, every selected GPU may receive a different model at once, allowing a bottleneck GPU to shed pressure without requiring any destination GPU to temporarily absorb an infeasible intermediate state.

For each round, select from every nonempty GPU the model whose removal gives the greatest lexicographic improvement in the full descending KVPR vector. Temporarily remove all selected models, reject the round if any remaining assignment is invalid, build a destination cost matrix from the exact global objective after inserting each removed model into each destination, forbid memory-invalid edges, and solve a bottleneck assignment by thresholding candidate objective values and applying deterministic augmenting-path matching. Accept only an assignment whose complete sorted KVPR vector is strictly better than the incumbent vector; retain all model identities and reject every memory-invalid insertion. Expected-gain check: this exposes feasible simultaneous cyclic reassignment vectors that the present greedy construction cannot create after completion; the falsifiable evaluator threshold is a `combined_score > 26.255972` while preserving `success_rate = 1`.

strategies.title: [multilevel-pressure-coarsening] Coarsen pressure-compatible models, optimize, a
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: multilevel-pressure-coarsening

Replacement scope: Replace the four fixed greedy construction orders with a multilevel seed-generation phase; keep the existing objective, incumbent fallback, and final threshold MILP phase.

Compute budget: At most 3 coarsening levels, at most 2 coarsened seeds per level, and at most 20 deterministic uncoarsening repair moves per seed; expected evaluation-time effect is moderate and bounded, with fewer items than the original greedy pass at every coarsened level.

Gain mechanism: The current constructors decide every model independently, so early placement of small high-pressure models can consume the slack needed by later large models. Coarsening introduces a different representation: pairs with similar pressure-to-size behavior are temporarily treated as indivisible composite items. The resulting placement makes global decisions about groups rather than individual items, then uncoarsening restores the original models and permits exact KVPR-improving repairs. This can cross packing barriers where neither member of a useful pair would be placed on the same GPU by the original independent greedy trajectory.

Sort models by pressure density and size, then greedily pair adjacent models only when their combined size is at most 80 GB and their combined pressure is finite. Repeat at most three times to form composite items carrying summed size, pressure, and original-member lists. Run the normal minimax greedy placement on each coarsened instance, expand composites back to original models, and perform bounded exact single-model relocation and swap repairs using the original KVPR formula. Every composite is assigned exactly once, expansion assigns every original model exactly once, and every construction or repair rejects total GPU memory above 80 GB. Expected-gain check: the new composite-item representation permits placements unreachable by all four independent-item construction orders; the falsifiable evaluator threshold is a `combined_score > 26.255972` with no failed placement instances.

strategies.title: [pheromone-feasible-construction] Learned stochastic construction from elite fea
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: pheromone-feasible-construction

Replacement scope: Replace the fixed list of four deterministic `orders` and associated seed selection with an elite-guided constructive search; retain the existing bounded MILP bisection as a final exact-feasibility improvement stage.

Compute budget: One deterministic baseline seed plus at most 10 ant-style construction starts, each visiting every model once; at most 3 elite placements retained; expected evaluation-time effect is linear in `gpu_num × len(models)` per start and lower than adding another MILP family.

Gain mechanism: The present seed space consists of only four globally sorted orders. Elite-guided construction changes the structural exploration space by learning model-to-GPU affinities from complete feasible placements while retaining exact objective-aware destination selection. It can reproduce useful co-location patterns discovered in one construction while varying other assignments, rather than merely changing a sort order or tie break.

Initialize affinity scores uniformly. At each start, order models by descending combination of size, pressure, and entropy of their current affinities. For each model, consider only GPUs with sufficient memory; rank them by the exact resulting descending KVPR vector, but sample deterministically from the best few using a cyclic low-discrepancy index weighted by affinity and inverse rank. Keep the best three complete feasible placements. After each completed placement, reinforce only its model-GPU assignments in proportion to inverse maximum KVPR and evaporate all older affinity weights by a fixed factor. Return the best exact objective vector seen, then allow the existing MILP bisection to improve it further. Every candidate destination is checked against 80 GB before assignment, and every model is inserted once. Expected-gain check: elite affinity creates model-specific GPU co-location choices absent from the incumbent’s four global orderings; the falsifiable evaluator threshold is a `combined_score > 26.255972` under the existing evaluator.

strategies.title: [threshold-evacuation-flow] Bottleneck GPU evacuation through a restricted feasi
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: threshold-evacuation-flow

Replacement scope: Replace the current post-construction candidate handling immediately before the global bisection block with a bottleneck-focused repair phase; retain the greedy construction and the final global MILP bisection fallback.

Compute budget: At most 3 repair rounds per incumbent; each round solves at most 2 restricted MILPs with a 0.10 second time limit. Expected evaluation-time effect: approximately +0.3 to +0.6 seconds on cases where SciPy is installed, no effect otherwise.

Gain mechanism: The incumbent’s global MILP can time out before finding a better incumbent, while its greedy seeds can strand several models together on one critical GPU. This repair directly permits a coordinated evacuation of several models from the current maximum-KVPR GPU into different recipient GPUs, a move that cannot be achieved by evaluating one model destination at a time.

For the current incumbent, identify all GPUs tied within a small numerical tolerance of the maximum KVPR. For each such source GPU, choose its assigned models as movable items and formulate a restricted binary assignment MILP with destinations equal to every other GPU plus the source. Fix all models outside the source GPU. At threshold `T = current_max_kvpr * (1 - 1e-5)`, require every destination GPU’s fixed transformed load plus moved transformed load to satisfy `sum(pressure + T * size) <= 80*T`, require memory capacity, and require each movable model to select exactly one destination. Solve first with all source models movable; if that is large, solve a second model restricted to the highest transformed-load models, while leaving lower-impact source models fixed. Decode only complete one-hot assignments, recompute all memory and KVPR values exactly, and retain only a strictly better valid candidate. The source model is not allowed to exceed memory after retained moves, and every destination receives only assignments satisfying the exact memory constraint.

Expected-gain check: this exposes coordinated source-to-many-destination evacuation assignments that the incumbent greedy placement cannot construct after its order is fixed; it is falsifiably useful only if hidden evaluation reports `combined_score > 26.255972` for the resulting strictly lower-max-KVPR incumbents.

strategies.title: [ordered-chain-partitioning] Contiguous pressure-memory chain dynamic-program se
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: ordered-chain-partitioning

Replacement scope: Replace the four-order greedy seed list with a seed generator that includes contiguous-chain dynamic-program placements, while retaining one existing greedy seed as a guaranteed feasible fallback and retaining later optimization phases.

Compute budget: At most 3 chain orderings; each uses an `O(gpu_num * n^2)` dynamic program and one backtracking pass. No optimizer starts. Expected evaluation-time effect: negligible for the small and medium batch instances expected by the current dense MILP formulation.

Gain mechanism: Existing constructions make independent per-model placement decisions and can produce interleaved, memory-fragmented assignments. A chain partition creates a different placement topology: models adjacent in a difficulty ordering are deliberately grouped into whole GPU segments, allowing the algorithm to balance cumulative numerator and denominator effects simultaneously rather than greedily committing individual models.

Build three deterministic model orders: descending `pressure + lambda*size`, descending `pressure/size` with large sizes breaking ties first, and descending size with pressure breaking ties first, where `lambda` is the global lower-bound threshold `sum(pressure) / (gpu_num*80 - sum(size))` when the residual is positive, otherwise zero. For each order, precompute prefix size and prefix pressure arrays. A segment from positions `a` through `b` is valid only if its size is at most 80, and its cost is its exact KVPR. Use dynamic programming where `dp[g][j]` is the minimum possible maximum segment KVPR after assigning the first `j` ordered models to `g` GPUs; try all valid final segment starts and retain predecessors. Permit empty GPU segments. Backtrack the best complete partition, recompute exact loads, and add it to the incumbent pool only when every model appears exactly once and every GPU satisfies memory capacity. This is a seed-only construction, so the existing MILP can improve it further.

Expected-gain check: chain partitions can yield a lower starting maximum than independent greedy placement whenever a beneficial contiguous grouping is blocked by earlier greedy choices; the concrete falsifiable threshold is an evaluated `combined_score > 26.255972` after the stronger seed tightens the MILP upper bound.

strategies.title: [orbitopal-threshold-search] Symmetry-reduced sparse exact threshold feasibility
strategies.plan:
Mechanism family: orbitopal-threshold-search

Replacement scope: Replace the current dense NumPy row construction inside the SciPy bisection block with a sparse constraint matrix and identical-GPU symmetry reduction; do not change the public function or greedy fallback.

Compute budget: One bisection search of at most 24 threshold probes, each with a 0.12 second HiGHS MILP time limit. Expected evaluation-time effect: lower matrix-construction cost and typically lower branch-and-bound cost; worst-case solver work is bounded at 2.88 seconds per placement call.

Gain mechanism: All GPUs are interchangeable, but the current MILP searches equivalent GPU relabelings and repeatedly allocates dense `n*gpu_num` vectors for every constraint. Pinning one deterministic anchor model to GPU 0 removes a factor of up to `gpu_num` equivalent placements without excluding any feasible unlabeled placement, and sparse construction leaves more of each time budget for finding actual feasible incumbents near the threshold.

Use the same fixed-threshold linearization already implied by KVPR: for each GPU, `sum((pressure[k] + T*size[k])*x[k,g]) <= 80*T`, alongside assignment and memory constraints. Select the anchor as the model with maximum `(size, pressure, index)` lexicographically and constrain it to GPU 0; because GPU identities are interchangeable, any feasible solution can be relabeled to satisfy this condition. Construct assignment, memory, and transformed-load coefficients as COO/CSR sparse arrays rather than dense rows. Use the greedy incumbent as the initial upper bound and the global residual-pressure lower bound `sum(pressure)/(gpu_num*80-sum(size))` when defined as the initial lower bound. Decode only one-hot feasible solutions and compare their recomputed exact KVPR against the incumbent.

Expected-gain check: the symmetry constraint preserves the exact feasible-placement set modulo GPU renaming while allowing more threshold probes within comparable runtime; it is falsifiably better only if its finer feasible threshold produces `combined_score > 26.255972`.

Gain mechanism: For a GPU with pressure `w` and used memory `u`, price adding model `k` by its exact marginal increase `((w+p[k]) / (80-u-s[k])) - (w / (80-u))`, rejecting nonpositive remaining memory. Select a conflict-free batch greedily by descending bid, allowing at most one incoming and one outgoing model per GPU in a round; apply the entire batch only if the recomputed sorted KVPR profile strictly improves. This simultaneous auction is not a sequence of single greedy placements: mutually beneficial moves that temporarily block one another are evaluated as one coordinated contact pattern.
